European Commission (2007). Reference Document on Best Available Techniques for the Manufacture of Large Volume Inorganic Chemicals - Solids and Others industry. Integrated Pollution Prevention and Control, August 2007. Seville: European IPPC Bureau.

Only the sodium chlorate section (s.7.13) has been extracted so far - the chlorate cell is a gap archetype and matters for Canadian pulp-bleaching chemical plants. Its figures come from CEFIC-Sodium Chlorate (2004). The other chapters (soda ash, titanium dioxide, carbon black, synthetic amorphous silica, inorganic phosphates, calcium carbide and the other 'specialty' processes) are queued; soda ash and carbon black have energy tables.
(1) The 'total energy' row is electricity only (AC kWh); steam use for crystallisation and drying is described but not quantified.
